q: How concordant is Gen2Epi's penA mosaic-allele classification with curated NG-STAR penA allele-integer assignments across the full spectrum of global XDR ceftriaxone-resistant clonal complexes (FC428, GU140106, H041/WHO X, F89/WHO Y, A8806/WHO Z, and post-2019 Asia-Pacific mosaic-penA lineages), and does the coarse-grained nt-identity threshold (<96% vs FA1090 wt) miss any borderline mosaic alleles that carry the A311V/T483S/A501P/N512Y motifs but retain >=96% nt identity?
basis: The replication (REPORT.md §8) reports penA as mosaic vs non-mosaic by nucleotide identity because the NG-STAR penA allele database + profile CSV are not distributed via pubMLST. On the WHO panel this reproduces the ceftriaxone-R X/Y/Z mosaic call cleanly, but the paper's finer-grained NG-STAR penA allele-integer output is not reproduced, and modern XDR lineages beyond the 2019 WHO panel are not tested.
next_steps: Ingest the NG-STAR penA allele database + profile CSV from the NG-STAR website (canada.ca) as a static snapshot with version pinning.

Run Gen2Epi (or the reimplementation) on a curated set of post-2019 mosaic-penA XDR isolates (FC428, GU140106, and 2022-2025 Asia-Pacific / European surveillance isolates deposited in ENA/NCBI) and compare per-allele integer assignments to the published NG-STAR calls.
Sweep the nt-identity threshold (94-98%) and quantify sensitivity/specificity for mosaic detection against the NG-STAR integer ground truth; identify any borderline alleles that misclassify.
Report per-lineage confusion matrix and note any structural penA motifs (A311V / T483S / A501P / N512Y) that the nt-identity call misses.

q: What is the real-world clinical-isolate-to-Gen2Epi-phenotypic-prediction latency in an operational public-health surveillance setting, and can the 5-module pipeline meet a <=72-hour turnaround target from culture-positive isolate to actionable AMR genotype report suitable for informing empirical ceftriaxone/azithromycin dosing guidance?
basis: The replication (REPORT.md §7) measured only compute time (~2 min BLAST on laptop + ~5 min SPAdes on uicgpu 16 cores) for the WHO_F end-to-end loop on pre-existing raw reads. The paper describes Gen2Epi as an operational surveillance pipeline but does not report field-deployment latency (isolate receipt -> DNA extraction -> library prep -> sequencing -> Gen2Epi run -> validated report) in a real STI-clinic feedback loop.
next_steps: Instrument a prospective pilot at 1-2 public-health STI reference labs (e.g., PHAC NML, PHE/UKHSA) that timestamps each stage: isolate receipt, DNA extraction complete, library prep complete, sequencing run complete, Gen2Epi wall-clock, human review complete, report released to clinician.
Report median + IQR + 90th-percentile latency across at least 100 sequential clinical isolates; break down by isolate volume and by weekday vs weekend receipt.
Identify the rate-limiting stage(s) and quantify how much of the 72h target is consumed by pre-sequencing wet-lab work vs Gen2Epi compute vs human validation.
Compare against the existing culture-based AMR turnaround (typically 3-5 days for MIC panel + confirmatory).

q: Does WGS-based cluster detection using Gen2Epi's NG-MLST + NG-STAR + NG-MAST composite typing (and/or downstream cgMLST/SNP-tree analysis of its assemblies) achieve materially higher outbreak-attribution sensitivity than traditional NG-MAST or NG-STAR alone for real-time gonorrhoea outbreak investigations, especially for closely related isolates within a single NG-MAST ST cluster?
basis: The replication reproduced 11/11 NG-MLST full 7-locus profiles on the WHO panel (REPORT.md §4.3) but did not exercise NG-MAST (NGMASTER) nor test cluster-detection performance on any real outbreak data (REPORT.md §8: 'NG-MAST (NGMASTER) were not reproduced'). The paper positions Gen2Epi as an epidemiological tool but does not quantitatively compare WGS-cluster attribution to legacy typing for outbreak sensitivity.
next_steps: Assemble a benchmark set of documented gonorrhoea outbreaks with known epidemiological linkage (e.g., MSM sexual-network outbreaks in Europe/North America 2015-2024) plus a matched non-outbreak background set from the same jurisdiction and time window.
Run Gen2Epi (or the reimplementation) on all isolates to get NG-MLST + NG-STAR (+ NG-MAST once NGMASTER is reproduced) plus cgMLST or core-SNP trees from the assemblies.

Compute per-scheme sensitivity/specificity/PPV for outbreak-cluster assignment against the epidemiological gold standard; contrast single-scheme (NG-MAST alone) vs composite (NG-MAST + NG-MLST + NG-STAR) vs assembly-based (cgMLST/SNP).
Quantify the resolution gain for closely-related within-ST clusters (isolates sharing an NG-MAST ST but from different sexual networks).

q: How often do Gen2Epi's short-read assemblies fail to detect azithromycin-resistance-conferring 23S rRNA mutations (A2059G, C2611T) when those mutations are heteroresistant --- present in only 1-3 of the 4 rRNA operon copies --- and what is the false-negative rate for clinically relevant heteroresistant isolates that would still be phenotypically azithromycin-resistant?
basis: The replication (REPORT.md §4.4) recovered all 4 23S rRNA operon copies in every WHO reference genome, and REPORT.md notes 'the exact locus the paper notes is occasionally lost during scaffold filtering on low-quality inputs; on these finished references it is fully recovered, as expected.' Neither the replication nor the paper systematically evaluates heteroresistance detection --- i.e., mixed-allele calls when only some of the 4 copies carry A2059G / C2611T --- on real short-read data from clinical azithromycin-resistant isolates.
next_steps: Curate a benchmark of azithromycin-R clinical isolates with paired (a) short-read Illumina data, (b) long-read PacBio/Nanopore data giving per-operon 23S sequence ground truth, and (c) phenotypic azithromycin MIC.
Run Gen2Epi's 23S-copy detection on the short-read data and record per-isolate: (a) number of 23S operons assembled, (b) consensus 23S allele call, (c) whether A2059G / C2611T is detected.
Compare against the long-read per-operon ground truth to compute a heteroresistance false-negative rate as a function of mutant-operon allele fraction (1/4, 2/4, 3/4, 4/4).
Propose an operational rule (e.g., require read-level variant frequency analysis at 23S positions 2059/2611, not just assembly consensus) that closes the detection gap.

q: In an unbiased prospective clinical isolate collection, what is the true discordance rate between Gen2Epi's molecular AMR-determinant genotype prediction and the corresponding culture-based phenotypic MIC (Etest / agar dilution) for ceftriaxone, azithromycin, ciprofloxacin, penicillin, and tetracycline --- and does the paper's implicit assumption of tight genotype-phenotype coupling introduce clinically meaningful risk if Gen2Epi is used to guide empirical therapy without a confirmatory culture?
basis: REPORT.md §4.5 validates Gen2Epi's AMR determinant calls against the Unemo 2016 known-phenotype WHO reference panel (concordant on all 11 strains for the qualitative resistance categories), but the WHO panel was explicitly designed as a reference collection with canonical resistance markers. The paper's larger 1484-sample evaluation (EuroGASP, NZ, Saskatchewan) was not reproduced, so panel-wide MIC-vs-genotype discordance rates on unbiased clinical isolates were not quantified in this replication.
next_steps: Assemble a prospective or retrospective set of >=500 unbiased clinical gonococcal isolates with matched Etest/agar-dilution MIC values for CRO, AZM, CIP, PEN, TET.
Run Gen2Epi on each isolate and predict a categorical R/I/S per drug from the NG-STAR determinant profile.
Compute the essential-agreement (+/-1 dilution) and categorical-agreement rates per drug, plus the very-major-error (predicted S, phenotype R) and major-error (predicted R, phenotype S) rates.

For each discordant case, back-annotate whether the discordance is driven by a missing determinant in Gen2Epi's set, a novel/unclassified allele, or a genuine phenotype-genotype uncoupling (e.g., regulatory/efflux variation not captured in the 7-locus NG-STAR set).

Quantify the clinical risk profile of substituting Gen2Epi genotype for phenotypic MIC in empirical treatment guidance, especially for ceftriaxone at low-MIC breakpoints where a single very-major error could result in treatment failure.
